name: Hand Off
tagline: Delegate the work — keep the outcome
about: Hand Off helps overloaded leads write delegation briefs that come back right the first time, set the right level of autonomy, hand over whole areas for good and recover gracefully when delegated work goes sideways.
persona: You are a pragmatic operations leader who learnt delegation the hard way: you optimise for clarity of outcome, explicit authority levels and the fewest check-ins that still catch problems early.

onboarding.title: Get it off your plate — properly
onboarding.subtitle: Tell Hand Off about your team so briefs match the people who'll receive them.

tools.title: Write a delegation brief
tools.subtitle: Outcome, constraints, authority, check-ins

inputs.label: The task
inputs.placeholder: own the vendor renewal for our analytics tool

inputs.label: To whom
inputs.placeholder: Priya, junior analyst, first time doing this

inputs.label: Deadline & constraints
inputs.placeholder: by the 30th, budget flat, legal must review

tools.prompt: Write a delegation brief for '{task}' handed to {to} with deadline and constraints: {deadline}. Sections: kv (Outcome — what done looks like, Why it matters, Constraints, Authority — what they decide alone, Escalate when, Check-in dates); a quote with a 120-word message to send them; a checklist of what the delegator must hand over (context, access, contacts, prior decisions); and a callout listing the questions to ask them before they start so nothing is assumed.

tools.title: Set the autonomy level
tools.subtitle: How much rope for this person and task

inputs.label: Person and their track record
inputs.placeholder: Marco, senior, strong but new to client work

inputs.label: Task and its risk
inputs.placeholder: presenting the quarterly review to our biggest client

tools.prompt: Recommend an autonomy level for {person} on: {task}. Sections: a table (Level | Name — Do as told / Recommend then act / Act then inform / Act alone / Own it | Fit for this case | Risk) covering all five with the recommended row marked; text explaining the recommendation in three sentences; steps for a check-in rhythm proportionate to the risk; and a quote with how to state the level to them explicitly.

tools.title: Hand over a whole area
tools.subtitle: Transfer ownership for good

inputs.label: What you're handing over
inputs.placeholder: the weekly metrics review and our vendor relationships

tools.prompt: Plan a {weeks}-week handover of '{area}' to {to} so the user never has to take it back. Sections: a table (Week | They do | I do | Who else needs telling) moving from shadowing to owning; a checklist of knowledge to transfer (decisions I make and why, contacts, recurring dates, the traps); a quote with the message announcing the new owner to stakeholders; and a callout on the signs the handover is quietly reverting.

tools.title: It came back wrong
tools.subtitle: Recover without taking it back

inputs.label: What came back and what's wrong
inputs.placeholder: the deck is 40 slides, wrong numbers on 3, and it's due tomorrow

inputs.label: Your honest guess at the cause

tools.prompt: Delegated work came back wrong: {what}. Suspected cause: {cause}. Sections: text with a blunt diagnosis of which part is on the delegator; steps for the next 24 hours that fix the deliverable without the user silently redoing it; a quote with the feedback conversation opener (behaviour, impact, ask); and bullets on what to change in the next brief.

tools.title: Weekly delegation check
tools.subtitle: Am I still hoarding?
tools.prompt: Run a weekly delegation self-check for the profile (team, size, stated habit). Sections: a checklist of 8 yes/no questions about the past week (e.g. did anything land on me that someone else could have owned); a table (Warning sign | What it usually means | This week's fix) tailored to the profile's stated habit; and a quote with one commitment sentence for next week.
